original_question: Among hamiltonian graphs on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length, what is the maximum possible number of edges?
target_in_paper: Problem 1.12 (Markström [27]) in Section 1 (“Erdös Problem 1”): determine the maximum number of edges in a Hamiltonian graph on n vertices with no repeated cycle lengths.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact graph class (Hamiltonian graphs on n vertices), the exact restriction (no two cycles have the same length), and the exact extremal objective (maximize the number of edges). It is very close to the paper’s official formulation and essentially matches Problem 1.12.
missing_details: The quantifier should be made explicit: the problem is asked for each integer n (implicitly n >= 3).
The phrase “no two cycles have the same length” should be spelled out as: for any two distinct cycles C and C' in the graph, |C| != |C'|.
For a fully stand-alone statement, it helps to write the problem as an extremal-function maximum over all Hamiltonian n-vertex graphs, rather than only in prose.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 3, determine the maximum possible value of |E(G)| over all Hamiltonian graphs G on n vertices such that any two distinct cycles of G have different lengths.
justification: The draft is already essentially the paper’s exact target. In Section 1 the authors first discuss the broader Erdős problem for f(n), the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph with pairwise distinct cycle lengths, including Theorem 1.3. They then record the Hamiltonian variant as Problem 1.12: “Determine the maximum number of edges in a hamiltonian graph on n vertices with no repeated cycle lengths.” So the refined question should stay narrowly focused on this Hamiltonian extremal problem and only make the quantifier on n and the meaning of “no repeated cycle lengths” fully explicit.
